name: Keyv
solves: Provides a unified key-value storage API with TTL-based expiry across multiple backends (in-memory, Redis, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, SQLite, Memcache), allowing developers to swap storage engines without changing application code.
best_for: Applications that need a simple get/set/delete caching API with TTL support without committing to a specific backend
Projects that want to start with in-memory caching and migrate to Redis or PostgreSQL later without code changes
Multi-backend caching where different environments use different stores (e.g., SQLite in dev, Redis in production)
HTTP response caching middleware that needs a pluggable cache store (e.g., cacheable-request uses Keyv)
Lightweight key-value persistence in CLI tools or small services where a full ORM is overkill
skip_when: You need advanced Redis features like pub/sub, streams, Lua scripting, or cluster-aware operations
You need a full-featured caching framework with multi-tier caching, cache stampede protection, or tag-based invalidation
Your application requires high-throughput caching with minimal overhead — the abstraction layer adds latency compared to using a Redis client directly
You only ever need in-memory caching with LRU eviction — a dedicated LRU cache library is lighter and faster
